batch_strategy: Select all 32 experiments now using the packet's unchanged premeasurement predictions. Prioritize controlled tests of endpoint-specific loading and solvent response, follow recent failures in both error directions, and test structural transfer boundaries in donor, carbonyl, ether, and early-eluting aromatic families. Use CW distance and quantile spans as supporting evidence, without treating them as calibrated epistemic uncertainty.

choices.reason: Cinnamic acid m173 at 2/1 retains the 124.75 mg loading and 1500 uL loading-solvent volume of 65fcce0299e031dedeb8. That observation finished at 78.37 mL, whereas this row predicts 50.72 mL. It tests whether completion actually decreases beyond 1/1 or the newly retrained curve still has an unsupported maximum.

m173 at 5/1 completes a fixed-loading, fixed-loading-solvent-volume extension from measured 0/1 and 1/1 records 87da8c37b16d810331a2 and 65fcce0299e031dedeb8. Together with the selected 2/1 row, its 9.52/46.78 mL prediction tests the shape of this unresolved completion response rather than imposing monotonicity.

m173 at 1/1 and 2000 uL loading solvent nearly matches the mass of 65fcce0299e031dedeb8 at 1500 uL. The model predicts similar completion, 77.11 mL, although the near-matched 0/1 records 6802f0b28c5a0c7b4c2a and 87da8c37b16d810331a2 differed by 18.39 mL. This tests whether the recorded volume association depends on eluent.

m209 at 10/1 and 68.75 mg starts a controlled lower-loading 10/1-to-20/1 comparison. Its predicted 7.62/31.18 mL probes the transition between the modest 5/1 completion in edfbbb86c05a0aeb1bfb and the much later 20/1 completion in 29b39881584c4fec1c58; those measured anchors used 206.25 mg.

m209 at 20/1 and 68.75 mg pairs with the selected 10/1 row and directly contrasts with 29b39881584c4fec1c58 at 206.25 mg under otherwise identical recorded conditions. The 15.65/53.69 mL prediction tests whether the recent phenol completion correction transfers across a threefold loading change.

Iodophenol m208 at 50/1 and 278.595 mg extends the exact loading conditions of bc62be727bf6ded3d86e at 5/1, measured at 9.02/16.66 mL. Its 25.42/48.72 mL prediction tests whether weak-eluent phenol growth resembles m209's newly measured steep completion or remains substituent-specific.

Trimethoxybenzene m110 at 20/1 and 112.6 mg supplies the same-loading anchor missing from the recent 50/1 measurement ce39d1762993bbbafaca. It also directly contrasts with fea75df17d0bf593243f at 56.3 mg. This separates loading from the completion growth previously observed with both conditions changing.

m19 at 1/1 and 46.1 mg contrasts with 9a60cb4735780275034e at 92.2 mg and connects to the same-loading 2/1 observation 6d21e9ec887b3408c612. The latter revealed a substantially delayed low-loading onset. This label tests whether that onset sensitivity persists in stronger eluent.

m19 at 1/1 and 138.3 mg completes the low/middle-observed/high-loading comparison and connects to 906bd247e050658f99d8 at 2/1. Its prediction is nearly identical to the selected low-loading row. Measuring both can distinguish eluent-dependent onset sensitivity from the almost flat completion response measured at 2/1.

m72 at 10/1 and 153.3 mg directly contrasts with 7383949c431e18f39597 at 51.1 mg, holding DCM and its 200 uL volume fixed. The model predicts 12.53/33.82 mL, close to the measured lower-loading endpoints. This tests loading sensitivity on the relatively flat side of the newly resolved transition.

m72 at 20/1 and 153.3 mg pairs with its selected 10/1 row and directly contrasts with 1b1a9ec85268aa66d327 at 51.1 mg, measured at 36.42/112.07 mL. This completes a loading-by-eluent rectangle and tests whether the sharp completion increase remains similar across a threefold mass change.

Ethyl nicotinate m90 at 2/1 and 166.05 mg directly contrasts with 6a4e95d2a3cca31094a1 at 55.35 mg, measured at 16.89/29.23 mL. It also anchors the same-loading response toward b51b5dbcd2a38b174973 at 5/1. This tests whether m19's strong onset loading effect transfers to a chemically different basic nitrogen scaffold.

m169 at 20/1 fills the fixed-122 mg gap between 9b11493847c035abf800 at 10/1 and f46da3c00b2199795e4c at 50/1. Those labels showed onset near 6–7 mL while completion increased from 17.48 to 36.16 mL, rejecting the previous uniformly delayed prediction. This tests completion curvature after that repair.

Meta-methylbenzaldehyde m142 at 50/1 predicts 18.11/42.40 mL, later than dimethylbenzaldehyde 8b06ec38a7e5999edfa6 at close loading in PE with the same loading-solvent volume. Paired with the selected 10/1 point, it tests whether the model's steeper substitution-specific response is real.

m142 at 10/1 establishes the other end of the fixed-101.9 mg curve. Its 6.37/16.38 mL prediction is close to the measured dimethylbenzaldehyde point c8b332c6c452d13fcc6e under comparable loading and identical PE/300 uL loading-solvent conditions. Two labels identify where their response curves diverge.

Naphthaldehyde m195 at 50/1 predicts 21.08/51.41 mL, extending the 20/1 observation 783cf2454912fc14bb80 at 100 mg. Related brominated m196 finished at 28.38 mL with an early onset in 7c6e7b244de393e8554d. This tests carbonyl transfer across fused-ring substitution, acknowledging loading and loading-solvent-volume differences.

Bromobenzofuran m8 at 20/1 and 235.95 mg extends the exact loading conditions of bb387f1af7263b2445fb at 5/1, measured at 4.70/15.90 mL. Its 14.20/32.51 mL prediction begins a controlled test of the steep curve assigned to this neutral aromatic oxygen scaffold.

m8 at 50/1 pairs with its selected 20/1 row at identical loading conditions. The model predicts further growth to 21.81/51.17 mL. Measured bromobenzodioxole b94677e12c4d6aa11d9b and bromonaphthalene ba5381d85ba24754040c provide modest-retention structural references, with their different loadings retained as limitations.

Methoxynaphthalene m124 at 50/1 and 106.4 mg extends the same-loading 10/1 observation 2fa282eae76354cf9096, measured at 4.93/12.39 mL. Its predicted 9.10/18.04 mL supplies a neutral ether comparator for the selected m8 curve and tests transfer across fused versus exocyclic oxygen connectivity.

Thiol-containing ester m96 at 20/1 and 178.05 mg extends the exact loading conditions of 0be038db2251642c6862 at 10/1, measured at 12.48/18.58 mL. The predicted 19.55/39.71 mL tests whether this sulfur donor develops the steep weak-eluent growth associated with some alcohols.

m96 at 50/1 completes the selected fixed-loading 10/1-observed, 20/1, 50/1 curve. Its predicted 27.74/63.54 mL is a substantial unmeasured extension. The pair tests a donor-identity transfer boundary rather than assuming that equal HBD counts imply similar silica response.

Acetophenone oxime m11 at 20/1 and 100 mg supplies the same-loading intermediate anchor for its selected 50/1 row. Observation 1182373ab8814dbe2f43 at 5/1 exposed overprediction, while a38fee52661fd3e3b7ea at 20/1 used 150 mg. This tests the response of an oxime rather than transferring a generic nitrogen correction.

m11 at 50/1 predicts 31.57/78.98 mL and pairs with its selected 20/1 point at identical loading conditions. Its hydroxyl/nitrogen connectivity differs from both pyridines and the NH-containing enamine m72. The labels test where steep nitrogen- or donor-associated response features generalize.

Methyl anthranilate m104 at 20/1 and 116.8 mg extends its measured 2/1 anchor 04e994913bc43aa60007 and the lower-loading 5/1 record 9333d130f52d80332cf0. Its 17.07/39.64 mL prediction can be compared with ethyl anthranilate fe40c32169d87261e1e9, while acknowledging different loading solvents and volumes.

Tertiary alcohol m51 at 10/1 and 144.9 mg forms a near-mass-matched structural comparison with the selected secondary alcohol m60 under identical PE/300 uL loading-solvent conditions. Its 29.06/43.13 mL prediction tests OH steric environment and connectivity; a1ea7a9303a5fc7a7b0f supplies lower-loading 2/1 context.

Secondary alcohol m60 at 10/1 and 145.5 mg matches the loading conditions of c5594361764ec76761e2 at 1/1 and closely matches the selected m51 row. The predicted 27.19/39.86 mL tests whether the two nonbenzylic OH environments behave similarly, despite the disparate measured benzylic alcohol curves elsewhere.

Cyclic tertiary alcohol m203 at 10/1 and 150 mg extends the exact loading conditions of eb151126b40eda411ab7 at 5/1, measured at 9.52/14.71 mL. Its 23.45/31.01 mL prediction establishes the intermediate point of a controlled donor-environment response curve.

m203 at 20/1 pairs with its selected 10/1 row and the measured same-loading 5/1 anchor eb151126b40eda411ab7. The model predicts 39.30/55.83 mL. This tests whether a sterically encumbered cyclic alcohol really follows this steep response and helps prevent indiscriminate transfer from primary alcohol failures.

Dimethyl acetylenedicarboxylate m91 at 50/1 and 211.8 mg matches the loading conditions of a93680d827624e459a39 at 10/1, measured at 6.62/11.41 mL. The current 5.36/4.50 mL prediction reverses endpoint order. This label tests an underconstrained weak-eluent region without presuming that every recorded endpoint inconsistency has the same cause.

Pentafluorobenzene m156 at 5/1 and 75.7 mg predicts 9.44/6.94 mL, also reversing endpoint order and placing onset later than measured 50/1 record 8fa8d7ec035c6a829dc4. Together with the ordered 1/1 observation bd2d2667de61e29eaea3 at higher loading, this tests a distinctive aromatic response-shape warning.

Previously unmeasured m138 at 50/1 has low maximum similarity to observed molecules and predicts early elution at 4.08/11.70 mL. It tests transfer across combined methyl, fluoro, and iodo substitution in the numerous low-retention aromatic rows. Recent m50 accuracy in 7b5ad733102ce39fbb82 cautions against assuming novelty implies failure.

Previously unmeasured diiodobenzene m157 at 50/1 predicts 8.76/12.26 mL with a recorded 900 uL DCM loading volume. It extends early-eluting heavy-halogen coverage and tests whether increased halogen substitution and this loading condition transfer correctly. Dibromonaphthalene 6344eef305d5c2c9e159 showed a useful completion overprediction, but does not establish this row's error.

hypotheses.content: Loading effects depend on scaffold, eluent, and endpoint. The completed m19 triplet shows a strong onset shift with little completion change; m103 has nearly unchanged onset and a small positive completion response. m128 and m13 also separate onset from completion, while m205 demonstrates that completion can change materially with mass. A universal loading correction is inadequate.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Many candidate predictions remain nearly loading-insensitive. Controlled rectangles can teach conditional onset and completion effects while preserving the genuinely small responses measured in other scaffolds.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does m19's onset sensitivity persist at 1/1, does m72's loading response differ across its 10/1-to-20/1 transition, and do nicotinate, m209, and m110 show similar endpoint distinctions?

hypotheses.content: Carbonyl and neutral oxygenated-aromatic solvent responses depend on connectivity and substitution, and can affect completion more than onset. Recent m169 and m196 labels reject uniformly delayed weak-eluent predictions, whereas m134 and m110 show real completion growth. These observations support structural boundaries rather than one steep or flat response for the whole family.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The batch tests where recent corrections transfer and where they produce excessive extrapolation or excessive flattening. Paired response measurements also distinguish onset delay from a growing elution interval.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do m142, m195, and bromobenzofuran follow their predicted steep weak-eluent responses, and does methoxynaphthalene remain substantially more modest?

hypotheses.content: Nitrogen-containing scaffolds have distinct response transitions. m72 is nearly flat in completion from 5/1 to 10/1 but rises sharply by 20/1. The matched amino-nitrile isomers are similar at 2/1, despite their differences at 5/1. Pyridyl esters, anthranilates, tertiary-amine acrylates, enamines, and oximes therefore require connectivity-dependent responses rather than a nitrogen-presence correction.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Locating transitions and testing chemically distinct nitrogen environments can improve interpolation across solvent regimes without disturbing corrected neutral-nitrile behavior.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does the oxime exhibit the predicted weak-eluent growth, and does methyl anthranilate transfer the measured response of its ethyl analogue under their different recorded loading conditions?

hypotheses.content: Cinnamic acid has a strongly endpoint-specific response that is incompletely resolved across PE/EA and recorded loading-solvent volume. Its measured completion increases from 31.91 mL at 0/1 to 78.37 mL at 1/1 under fixed 1500 uL loading conditions, rejecting the previous predicted decrease. The near-mass-matched 0/1 volume comparison also differs substantially, but that association could be condition-dependent or record-specific.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The largest recent completion error occurred here. Additional controlled labels can distinguish a transferable condition interaction from a local anomaly, without introducing unrecorded pH, concentration, or flow explanations.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does completion really decline at 2/1 and 5/1, and does changing loading-solvent volume from 1500 to 2000 uL affect completion at 1/1 as it did in the near-matched 0/1 records?

hypotheses.content: Donor-containing compounds require structure- and endpoint-dependent solvent responses. m209 shows much stronger completion growth than previously predicted, while the bromohydroxyaldehydes retain comparatively early onset and reject the predicted 10/1 onset maxima. Alcohol connectivity, steric environment, and donor identity are plausible transfer boundaries; the observations do not establish their adsorption mechanisms.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The selected phenol, alcohol, and thiol measurements test transfer of recent donor corrections and protect against assigning all HBD-containing structures the same steep curve.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does m209 preserve its transition at lower loading, how steep is iodophenol's weak-eluent response, and do the matched secondary/tertiary alcohol comparison and cyclic-alcohol/thiol curves expose distinct donor-environment effects?

hypotheses.content: Endpoint-order reversals and unusual response shapes are useful model warnings, but are not established candidate errors. Some measured records themselves have V1 slightly or substantially above V2, so current reversals for m91 and m156 could reflect sparse condition coverage, endpoint underfitting, or inherited record inconsistencies. Their causes remain untested.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Targeted labels can repair underconstrained early-eluting endpoint relationships without assuming that a broad quantile span identifies epistemic uncertainty or that every anomalous recorded curve should be replaced by a physical rule.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: What endpoint order is measured for m91 at 50/1, and does m156 at 5/1 really have the predicted late onset relative to its measured weak-eluent point?

feedback_interpretation: The latest outcomes strengthen conditional response experiments and expose failures in both directions. m209 completion was underestimated by 19.65 mL at 20/1 and 42.67 mL at 50/1; m72 was close to flat from 5/1 to 10/1 but finished at 112.07 mL at 20/1, 44.40 mL above its acquisition prediction. Conversely, m169 at 50/1 had onset/completion overpredictions of 31.10/40.42 mL and actually retained an early onset while completion increased. m196 also remained early in onset. The proposed 10/1 onset maxima for m186 and m190 were not observed, so I reject that particular prediction-based hypothesis. Cinnamic acid's predicted completion decrease from 0/1 to 1/1 was decisively rejected: completion increased from 31.91 to 78.37 mL at fixed loading and loading-solvent volume. Its near-matched 0/1 volume comparison motivates testing an interaction, without establishing causality or a mechanism. The m19 loading triplet now shows onset falling from 23.69 to 16.43 to 13.39 mL while completion stays near 33–35 mL. The completed m103 rectangle instead shows almost unchanged onset and small positive completion shifts with mass. m205 weakens the earlier suggestion of preserved completion: increasing loading from 49.5 to 99 mg increased completion by 8.66 mL. The m128 pair further shows that weaker eluent can advance onset while delaying completion. The matched amino-nitrile isomers were similar at 2/1, resolving that local question and reducing the need for another immediate positional comparison. Dibromonaphthalene exposed a 7.68 mL completion overprediction, whereas branched arylalkyl chloride was close to prediction; novelty and numerical spans remain imperfect acquisition signals. These are historical acquisition errors, not current-model residuals.
batch_rationale: The batch combines local experiments that answer different unresolved questions. The acid series tests the largest recent failure and the remaining predicted completion maximum, with a near-matched loading-solvent-volume contrast. The m19 and m72 rectangles determine whether loading changes interact with solvent regime and affect onset differently from completion; m90, m209, and m110 test how those relationships transfer. Carbonyl and neutral-ether measurements follow both overprediction and underprediction, using fixed-loading curves and related structures to constrain excessive extrapolation without flattening genuine growth. Phenol, alcohol, thiol, and oxime measurements test functional-group interactions and structural environments rather than a blanket polarity or HBD correction. The two previously unmeasured halogenated aromatics add targeted coverage of the numerous early-eluting rows, while m91 and m156 test explicit endpoint-order warnings. Several candidates already have narrow V2 quantile spans or corrected-looking predictions; their value comes from discriminating condition and structural relationships, not from a numerical uncertainty quota. Paired rows are retained where they identify a slope or interaction, and duplicate rows with equivalent recorded conditions are not selected together. This may improve overall Row-distribution accuracy by teaching when corrections should transfer, when they should remain scaffold-specific, and how V1 and V2 respond separately. Missing experimental variables and possible record heterogeneity limit mechanistic interpretation; elution interval width remains distinct from predictive uncertainty.
